answer: An agent economy can make reputation nontransferable by tying it to a unique, stake-bearing account whose history accrues only through completed work and verified counterparties. For example, an oasis marketplace could require a quartz-backed deposit before an agent accepts a task, then release it only after the buyer confirms delivery or arbitration resolves a dispute. Spawning identities does not multiply useful reputation: each starts at zero, and each deposit locks capital the attacker risks losing for misconduct. A mesa of fake accounts therefore costs real funds and time to mature.
